parameters.description: Config.
parameters.name: config

keyterms.description: Words or phrases that the speech recognizer should prioritize.

noise_suppression.description: Noise suppression applied to incoming audio. Use `off` to disable it, `auto` for the default level, or `max` for stronger suppression.

background_sound.description: Background audio played during the conversation. Set to `null` to disable it.

file_id.description: ID of the audio file to play in the background.

emotion.description: Text-to-speech emotion supported by the selected voice and model, such as `calm`, `happy`, or `sad`.

pronunciation_dictionary_id.description: ID of the pronunciation dictionary used for agent speech.

speed.description: Speech speed multiplier, from `0.6` to `1.5`. Set to `null` to use the default speed.

voice_id.description: ID of the voice used for agent speech.

volume.description: Speech volume multiplier, from `0.5` to `2`. Set to `null` to use the default volume.

dynamic_variable_placeholders.description:
Sample values for Playground test calls. Production calls never use them.

Replaces saved samples on update. Omit to keep them, or send `{}` to clear them.

Variable names are case-sensitive, up to 64 characters, and use letters, digits, or underscores. Start with a letter or underscore; `system__` and `secret__` prefixes are reserved. Limited to 16 KiB of UTF-8 JSON.

initial_message.description: Message the agent says when the conversation begins. Set to `null` to wait for the user to speak first.

initial_message_interruptions.description: Controls how the agent handles interruptions while `initial_message` plays. `allow` lets the caller interrupt it, `ignore` plays it in full and adds what the caller says meanwhile to the LLM context without answering it, and `respond_after` plays it in full, then replies. Defaults to `allow`.

instructions.description: Instructions that define the agent's behavior. Supports dynamic variables such as `{{name}}`.

additional.description:
Other languages the caller can switch to, in order. Each is a language, such as `fr`, or a locale, such as `es-MX`. Omit or send `[]` for a single-language agent.

- When other languages are configured, the primary and additional languages must be English (`en`), Spanish (`es`), French (`fr`), Hindi (`hi`), or Japanese (`ja`), or supported locales of these languages.
- Each base language may appear only once, including the primary. For example, `en-US` and `en-GB` cannot be configured together.

Speech recognition listens for all configured languages. The agent switches when the caller asks and keeps using that language until another requested switch. A short phrase in another language does not trigger a switch.

presets.description: Settings per language, keyed by a language or locale such as `es-MX`. A preset applies only when the agent speaks that exact language or locale, including the primary language. A language without a matching preset uses the agent's voice and reads numbers, dates, times, and currency by its conventions. Omit or send `{}` for none.

primary.description: The language the agent starts each call in. Use a language code such as `en`, or a locale such as `en-US` for a regional accent. Write `initial_message` in this language. Omit or set to `null` to use `en`.

fallback_strategy.description: Models to fall back to when the primary model fails before it starts responding. `auto` uses Cartesia-managed fallback models. `explicit` uses up to three model IDs from `GET /v1/agents/models`, in order. Set to `null` to disable fallback. Defaults to `auto`.

id.description: Model ID from `GET /v1/agents/models`.

max_output_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens the model can generate, from `1` to `4096`. Set to `null` for no limit.

temperature.description: Controls the randomness of model responses, from `0` to `1`.

prompt_optimization.description: Optimizes the system prompt with guidelines for natural and realistic speech. Defaults to `true`.

speculative_generation.description: Starts LLM generation on an eager end-of-turn prediction to reduce response latency. Defaults to `true`.

system_tools.description: Built-in tools available to the agent.

end_call.description: Configuration for ending the call. Omit or set to `null` to disable this tool.

description.description: What the tool does and when the agent should use it. Set to `null` to use the default system-optimized description.

pre_tool_speech.description: Controls whether the agent speaks before using the tool. `auto` lets the agent decide, `force` asks the agent to speak first, and `off` doesn't ask it to.

send_dtmf.description: Configuration for sending DTMF tones. Omit or set to `null` to disable this tool.

description.description: What the tool does and when the agent should use it. Set to `null` to use the default system-optimized description.

pre_tool_speech.description: Controls whether the agent speaks before using the tool. `auto` lets the agent decide, `force` asks the agent to speak first, and `off` doesn't ask it to.

skip_turn.description: Configuration for skipping the agent's turn. Omit or set to `null` to disable this tool.

description.description: What the tool does and when the agent should use it. Set to `null` to use the default system-optimized description.

pre_tool_speech.description: Controls whether the agent speaks before using the tool. `auto` lets the agent decide, `force` asks the agent to speak first, and `off` doesn't ask it to.

wait_timeout_secs.description: Temporary check-in timeout in seconds after skipping a turn. Set a longer timeout to give the caller more time, `-1` to disable check-ins, or `null` to keep normal timing. User speech or DTMF restores the original timeout. Requires check-ins to be enabled. The inactivity end-call timer keeps running.

transfer_to_number.description: Configuration for transferring the call. Omit or set to `null` to disable this tool.

description.description: What the tool does and when the agent should use it. Set to `null` to use the default system-optimized description.

pre_tool_speech.description: Controls whether the agent speaks before using the tool. `auto` lets the agent decide, `force` asks the agent to speak first, and `off` doesn't ask it to.

transfers.description: Phone numbers the agent can transfer a call to.

condition.description: When the agent should transfer the call to this destination.

phone_number.description: E.164 phone number or a single dynamic variable, such as `{{transfer_number}}`. Must resolve to a valid E.164 number when the tool runs.

voicemail_detection.description: Configuration for detecting voicemail. Omit or set to `null` to disable this tool.

description.description: What the tool does and when the agent should use it. Set to `null` to use the default system-optimized description.

message.description: Message spoken without interruption before hangup, even when `pre_tool_speech` is `off`. Set to `null` for no message.

pre_tool_speech.description: Controls whether the agent speaks before using the tool. `auto` lets the agent decide, `force` asks the agent to speak first, and `off` doesn't ask it to.

timezone.description: IANA time zone for `{{system__time}}`. Defaults to `UTC`.

id.description: ID of a tool from the Tools API.

inactivity_check_in_secs.description: Seconds of inactivity before the agent checks in, from `5` to `60`. Defaults to `8`. Set to `null` to disable check-ins. When enabled, it must be less than `inactivity_end_call_secs`.

inactivity_end_call_secs.description: Seconds of inactivity before the agent says a farewell message and ends the call, from `20` to `240`. Defaults to `240`; cannot be `null`.

See [Volume, Speed, and Emotion](/build-with-cartesia/capability-guides/volume-speed-emotion) for a guide on this option.

volume.description: Adjust the volume of the generated speech between 0.5x and 2.0x the default volume. Valid values are between [0.5, 2.0] inclusive.

schema.description: Additional fields to include in the response.

accents.description: Accents the voice sounds native in, with the original accent marked `is_native: true`. In any other [supported language](/build-with-cartesia/tts-models/latest#language-support), the voice speaks with that original accent. Only available for voices with known accent information.

items.description: One accent this voice sounds native in. `accent` is an accent id from [GET /accents](/api-reference/accents/list).

is_native.description: Whether this is the accent the voice was originally recorded in. It's the accent the voice falls back to when it speaks a language it has no matching accent for.

access.description: Who can use the resource. `private` means only the owner can use the resource. `public` means everyone can use the resource.

country.description: Deprecated. Prefer `accents[].locale` (BCP-47). ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code when available (e.g. `US`, `GB`, `FR`).

created_at.description: The date and time the voice was created.

description.description: A description for the voice, typically longer than the tagline if both are provided.

gender.description: The gender of the voice, if specified.

id.description: The ID of the voice. Find one in the [Voice Library](https://play.cartesia.ai/voices) or via [List Voices](/api-reference/voices/list).

is_owner.description: Whether your organization owns the voice.

is_pro.description: Whether this voice is a pro voice clone.

name.description: The display name of the voice. Does not include the tagline.

preview_file_url.description: A URL to download a preview audio file for this voice. Useful to avoid consuming credits when looking for the right voice. The URL requires the same Authorization header. Voice previews may be changed, moved, or deleted so you should avoid storing the URL permanently. This property will be null if there's no preview available. Only included when `expand[]` includes `preview_file_url`.

status.description: Status of the voice. Only active voices are returned in [List Voices](/api-reference/voices/list) by default unless `include_archived=true`.

tagline.description: A short descriptor for the voice (at most 32 characters). Empty string when unset.

visibility.description: When the resource is returned by the list endpoint. `owner` means the resource appears for the owner only. `all` means the resource appears for all users.

parameters.description: A cursor for pagination. Pass the ID of the first item from the previous page to fetch the previous page.

parameters.description: The maximum number of items to return, ranging between 1 and 100.

agent_id.description: The identifier of the agent associated with the call.

agent_version_id.description: The [agent version](/api-reference/agents/versions/get) used for the call, which is the version published when the call started.

dynamic_variables.description: Initial custom values while the call is active; final values after it ends, including webhook assignments. System variables are not included. Omitted from ZDR or redacted call history.

end_reason.description: The reason why the call ended.

end_time.description: The end time of the agent call.

error_message.description: The error message, if any, associated with the call.

id.description: The unique identifier for the agent call.

redacted_at.description: When the call's sensitive data was deleted, if it has been. Set by `DELETE /agents/calls/{call_id}`; deleted fields are omitted from responses.

start_time.description: The start time of the agent call.

status.description: The status of the agent call.

summary.description: A brief summary of the call, generated by Cartesia. Omitted when no summary was generated, e.g. when nobody spoke because the call was not answered or failed to connect.

telephony_account_type.description: The telephony account type backing the call. `cartesia` is the default Cartesia-hosted path; `twilio` indicates a customer-owned Twilio subaccount; `sip_trunk` indicates a customer-connected SIP trunk.

telephony_params.description: The telephony parameters associated with the call when the call is made via phone.

call_sid.description: The SID of the telephony call from the provider.

connection_type.description: The type of connection used for the call.

direction.description: The direction of the call, e.g., `inbound` or `outbound`.

from.description: The phone number of the agent. Present for phone calls; omitted for websocket connections.

headers.description: Additional headers associated with the telephony call.

parameters.description: Additional parameters associated with the telephony call.

to.description: The phone number of the caller. Present for phone calls; omitted for websocket connections.

transcript.description: The transcript of the agent call.

end_timestamp.description: The end timestamp in seconds relative to the start of the call.

ignored.description: Present and `true` on a `user` turn that ended while the agent's `initial_message` was playing with `initial_message_interruptions` set to `ignore`. The turn is in the LLM context, but the agent didn't answer it.

role.description: The role of the participant in the conversation. Roles are `user`, `assistant`, or `system`. `assistant` is the agent.

start_timestamp.description: The start timestamp in seconds relative to the start of the call.

stt_ttfb.description: The time to first byte in seconds for speech-to-text.

text.description: The text content of the transcript. This is the text that was spoken by the user or the agent.

tool_calls.description: The tool calls made during the turn.

tts_ttfb.description: The time to first byte in seconds from the agent for text-to-speech.

zdr_enabled.description: Whether [Zero Data Retention](/enterprise/zero-data-retention) was on for the call. When `true`, the transcript, recording, summary, and logs are not retained.

has_more.description: Whether there are more results available.

next_page.description: An ID that can be passed as `starting_after` or `ending_before` to get the next page of calls.

description: Cartesia non-streaming speech, voices, datasets, agents and calls.

cartesia_new_agents_trigger.description: Runs each time an agent is created in Cartesia. Ones created before the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields created_at, description, id, name, updated_at, version_id

cartesia_new_calls_trigger.description: Runs each time a call is created in Cartesia. Ones created before the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields id, agent_id, agent_name, agent_version_id, zdr_enabled, start_time, end_time, redacted_at, transcript, telephony_params.to, telephony_params.from, telephony_params.call_sid, telephony_params.direction, telephony_params.parameters, telephony_params.headers, telephony_params.connection_type, telephony_account_type, summary, status, error_message, end_reason, dynamic_variables

cartesia_new_datasets_trigger.description: Runs each time a dataset is created in Cartesia. Ones created before the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields id, name, created_at, description

cartesia_new_or_updated_agents_trigger.description: Runs for each agent added or changed in Cartesia. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on start it only when they change. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields created_at, description, id, name, updated_at, version_id

cartesia_new_or_updated_calls_trigger.description: Runs for each call added or changed in Cartesia. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on start it only when they change. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields id, agent_id, agent_name, agent_version_id, zdr_enabled, start_time, end_time, redacted_at, transcript, telephony_params.to, telephony_params.from, telephony_params.call_sid, telephony_params.direction, telephony_params.parameters, telephony_params.headers, telephony_params.connection_type, telephony_account_type, summary, status, error_message, end_reason, dynamic_variables

cartesia_new_or_updated_datasets_trigger.description: Runs for each dataset added or changed in Cartesia. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on start it only when they change. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields id, name, created_at, description

cartesia_new_or_updated_voices_trigger.description: Runs for each voice added or changed in Cartesia. Ones already there when the workflow is turned on start it only when they change. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields id, is_owner, status, access, name, tagline, description, gender, created_at, preview_file_url, language, accents, country, is_pro, visibility

cartesia_new_voices_trigger.description: Runs each time a voice is created in Cartesia. Ones created before the workflow is turned on don't start it. It can watch up to 4,000. How often it checks follows your workspace plan.

output.record: object with the fields id, is_owner, status, access, name, tagline, description, gender, created_at, preview_file_url, language, accents, country, is_pro, visibility
